findings.claim: error_fingerprint claims no-follow metadata of every watched input and none opened, but os.lstat('in/plan.md', dir_fd=...) follows an intermediate in/ symlink. An unreadable-at-start job whose in/ is a symlink is therefore fingerprinted by the outside target's inode and mtime, so an edit of that outside file breaks LD-70 backlog silence even though the unreadable condition (in/ is still a symlink) did not change. _open_job_file walks in/ with O_NOFOLLOW; the new fingerprint path does not.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import contextlib, io, os, sys, tempfile, time
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
sys.path.insert(0, 'ops/conductor/tools')
os.environ['LANE_CONF'] = str(Path('ops/lane.conf').resolve())
import watchdog
root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
store = root / 'dispatch'
job = store / '20260916T100000Z-code-grok-inlink'
job.mkdir(parents=True)
outside = root / 'outside'
outside.mkdir()
plan = outside / 'plan.md'
plan.write_text('secret\n')
(job / 'in').symlink_to(outside)
(job / 'record.json').write_text('{"id":"x","status":"closed","job":"check-tests"}\n')
a = SimpleNamespace(store=store, report_existing=False, no_forge=True, forge_every=1, heartbeat_every=99, warn_fraction=2/3, tick=1.0, once=False)
w = watchdog.Watch(a)
fp = w.startup_backlog[job.name][1]
plan_row = [r for r in fp if r[0] == 'in/plan.md'][0]
assert plan_row[2] == os.lstat(plan).st_ino
buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
    w.run_tick()
assert w.silent(job.name) and 'InputUnavailable' not in buf.getvalue()
time.sleep(0.02)
plan.write_text('secret2\n')
buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf):
    w.run_tick()
assert not w.silent(job.name)
assert 'InputUnavailable' in buf.getvalue() and 'deviation unavailable' in buf.getvalue()
print('ok')
PY
